interactions.rationale: Parsing, merge order and exact kind resolution meet before layout.
Sparse occupancy must not move or reinterpret fixed ports.
Low-use roots move inward while a common root and its routes remain readable.
Physical aliases must remain one logical source in every statistic.
Shared trunks must not multiply crossings while different nets remain attributable.
Tree normalization must preserve physical endpoint ports and must not merge distinct output-port networks.
Separately useful root aliases can overlap into a logical split-rejoin cycle; consolidation and tree normalization must compose without quality regression.
A physical single-edge root facility may need a continuous later column or a consumer-suffix corridor even when its logical root has high fanout.
A corridor translation can make a root alignment newly feasible; stale assessment or precise-search leakage can hide the bend or destroy scale.
Arbitrary glyph height and floating port coordinates meet facility replication and shared-trunk routing; fixed row charges or exact float equality can create duplicate roots or false detours.
A fan-in may cross before its target but still have a dominated tail; moving only the target can hit a sibling row, while over-expanding ownership can hide a true obstacle.
Endpoint correctness, obstacle clearance and final artifact paths can fail independently.
Preferences and free placement must never reverse a causal edge.
A one-to-two sink group beside a one-to-one group is a known crossing interaction.
Long/empty values and the lowest row affect final export bounds.
Quality measurement must remain feasible at the largest declared stress size.
The frozen and source archive must preserve the same input surface as the repository.
Offline quality guidance and its ledger must be present and hash-bound in the archive.
A feedback receipt or design metric that is missing, stale or only checks a trigger condition must stop release.
